note: Applies to EVERY category, not just one - checked against the item's properties block (not category_fields). See README.md.

base_value.note: Base economic / sale value in dollars ($). Mandatory on every item in the catalog.

weight_kg.note: Physical weight in kilograms (kg). Mandatory on every item in the catalog.

max_stack_size.note: Maximum inventory stack count (integer >= 1). Mandatory on every item in the catalog.

pack_quantity.label: Pack Quantity
pack_quantity.note: How many individual items this one stands for (a stack, pallet, case or bundle of N). The game SHOWS the name as 'Name xN' (then its weight, 'Name xN (9 kg)', when Show Weight In Name is on); keep the stored name plain ('Cement Bag Pallet', never 'Cement Bag (Pallet of 10)'). Leave empty for a single item.

build_speed.label: Build Speed
build_speed.note: Tools only: how fast building goes with this tool (1 = the baseline stage time of 30 s, 0.5 = twice as long, 2 = twice as fast). A stage takes as long as its slowest tool group allows, and each group uses the fastest of its tools that is at the site. Primitive tools (hammer, hand saw, shovel) are below 1; power tools are 1 or more. Empty = 1.

display_weight.label: Show Weight In Name
display_weight.note: Materials and packaged goods only: the game shows the name as 'Name (9 kg)' / 'Name (20 lb)', generated from weight_kg and converted by the Metric / Imperial setting. A pack (pack_quantity set) shows its quantity first, 'Name x10 (200 kg)'. Never type a weight into the name itself.

is_consumable.note: Whether the item is consumed / depleted upon use. Mandatory on every item in the catalog.

is_spawnable.note: Whether this asset is placed into the world during terrain generation. When true, the asset must also declare a 'spawning' block naming at least one target biome (spawning.biomes[]). When false or absent, the asset exists only as an inventory/crafting item and is never scattered by the generator. Defaults to false when omitted, so older manifests stay valid.

thirst_restore.note: score, same -100/+100 scale as the other player stats. Drinkable water containers and watery food/drink items only (positive). 0 for everything else.

energy_restore.note: score, same -100/+100 scale as the other player stats. Beds (full rest) and seating (couches/chairs, a lesser rest) only (positive). 0 for everything else.

stamina_restore.note: score, same -100/+100 scale as the other player stats - a shorter-term exertion resource, distinct from energy_restore's longer-term tiredness/sleep. Mainly food (quick energy from eating). 0 for everything else.

wellness_modifier.note: Wellness is the player's overall health/sickness meter, and it's broader than just consumption. Sources of wellness change, most of which are RUNTIME EVENTS/CONDITIONS rather than a static per-item value (so most items stay 0 here even though they're relevant to the mechanic): (1) consumption - contaminated/unfiltered water and questionable food lower it, clean filtered water and wholesome food raise it (this is what the field captures on food/water items); (2) injury - physical harm while doing risky work (e.g. handling an aggressive animal, see ranching.temperament) is a runtime event, not an item property; (3) environmental exposure - working in/near unclean conditions (manure piles, see waste category) lowers it via proximity, similar to happiness_modifier's proximity model; (4) sleep deprivation - insufficient energy_restore over time is a runtime accumulation, not a single item's value; (5) hygiene - NOT SHOWERING lowers wellness over time; there is currently NO shower/bathing item in the catalog to raise it back - this is a real gap, see the queued asset request; (6) WEATHER EXPOSURE - being out in hot sun without drinking (thirst_restore not being met) lowers wellness on top of the thirst penalty itself; being outside in cold/winter weather without adequate winter gear also lowers wellness. There is currently NO clothing/apparel category or winter gear item in the catalog at all - a real gap, see the queued Winter Coat asset request; once winter gear exists it should carry a positive wellness_modifier (or a dedicated cold-resistance field) representing protection from this penalty. DESIGN RULE: wellness can ONLY be raised by the player deliberately taking care of themselves (eating well, hydrating, sleeping, showering, avoiding injury/unclean exposure) - it must never passively regenerate on its own or rise from unrelated sources. RUNTIME REQUIREMENT: wellness itself should feed back into OTHER stats, not just be a dead-end meter - low wellness should reduce max stamina and reduce happiness. This cross-stat relationship is game logic, not a catalog field.

placeable.label: Placeable
placeable.note: Whether the player can put this item on the ground. Every item with a model can be placed; set false to forbid it (lights and panels that mount on a building are never placed on the ground). Delivery still sets down as itself only the items that declare true; the rest arrive in boxes. The first left click brings out a shadow preview, R rotates it, Enter or a second click places it. Seeds that plant a growth group are never placed.

stores.label: Sold At
stores.note: The phone shops that sell this item (depot, lumber, grocer, feed, water, vehicles, equipment, livestock, furniture, voltvision, trailershack). The manifest is the ONLY place this lives: the phone builds each shop from the catalog. Setting it makes the item buyable at base_value (is_buyable true).

sale_unit.label: Sale Unit
sale_unit.note: How a shop counts it: ea, kit, box, bale, packet, tank ... (default ea).

store_category.label: Shop Label
store_category.note: The chip label a shop shows for it when it differs from its asset category default (for example Trailer Parts).

store_overrides.label: Per-Shop Overrides
store_overrides.note: One shop that sells it differently: {"trailershack": {"category": "Trailer Repair", "unit": "ea", "price": 35}}. Edited in the manifest JSON.

support_surface.label: Carries Things (pallet)
support_surface.note: A placed one carries items on top (a pallet): things placed over its deck rest on it, packed side by side and stacked up to their stacking limit. A pallet that still carries things cannot be picked up. Needs placeable = true.

deck_heights.label: Shelf Heights (shelving unit)
deck_heights.note: A support_surface item with several shelves (a shelving unit): the height of each shelf's top face above the ground, in metres, lowest first, comma separated ("0.15, 0.62, 1.09, 1.56"). Point at the open front of a shelf to put things on that one. Empty = one deck at the model's height (a pallet).

stacking_limit.label: Stack Limit (placed)
stacking_limit.note: How many identical PLACED ones can be stacked on each other in one grid square in the world (bags of cement: 4). 1 or empty = they do not stack. Needs placeable = true. A container sets this in its container block instead (container.stacking_limit), which wins when both are set. It is not the toolbar stack size (max_stack_size).

attach_surface.label: Mounts On
attach_surface.note: An item that mounts on a FINISHED building instead of standing on the ground: wall (a breaker box, a wall sconce, a switch), ceiling (a ceiling light) or roof (a solar rack: aimed at the roof from the GROUND, there are no ladders; it lies on the roof surface with its long side up the slope). With the item in hand a left click brings out a preview over the walls / ceiling, a second click or Enter mounts it, a right click takes it down. Leave empty for everything else. Such an item is not placeable (placeable false). See docs/ATTACHED_ITEMS.md. Model: the back of a wall item is the plane y = 0 sticking out towards -y; a ceiling item hangs from its top.

builds_structure.label: Kit Builds Structure
builds_structure.note: A KIT: with it in hand a left click brings out the structure's preview (R turns it a quarter turn) and a second click starts its work site (the dirt area, the yard ring, the front arrow); the kit is used up. Structure id (a growth group of the structures category). The structure's own blueprint is then not for sale: the kit is how it is bought.

wire_role.label: Wiring Role
wire_role.note: A device the off-grid solar chain wires together (docs/WIRING.md): solar panel (the panel on its mount) > wall entry > DC breaker box > MPPT charge controller > battery > inverter, and an inverter feeds an AC panel (the outdoor breaker box); a bus bar joins any DC devices. With wire cutters in hand a right click on a device and then on another wires them (either order). propane_tank, propane_connector and propane_filler (a fill post for portable tanks) are the ends of a PROPANE line, joined the same way but with the pipe wrench and propane pipe. Empty = not wired. Water (docs/WELLS.md): water_tank, water_filter, water_inlet, water_spigot, water_pump, joined with the pipe wrench and PVC pipe. Sewage (docs/SEPTIC.md): sewer_outlet (a building's waste outlet), sewer_pump (a macerator), septic_tank, septic_dbox (a distribution box) and leach_field, joined with the pipe wrench and black waste pipe (wire_kind sewer). standby_generator: a propane standby generator, piped to a propane tank (pipe wrench) and wired with AC wire to a building's generator_lockout box (mounted outside): the box runs the building on its breaker box or on the generator, never both, switching over by itself when the power runs short. disconnect: a safety disconnect wired into a run (AC or DC); a right click throws it, and off it cuts the run there. fuel_tank (a bulk gasoline / diesel tank) and fuel_pump (an electric dispenser, also wired to a breaker box with AC wire) are joined with the pipe wrench and a fuel line (wire_kind fuel).

wire_kind.label: Wire Kind
wire_kind.note: A coil or spool of wire: dc_indoor (red and black, for the runs inside), dc_outdoor (weather-rated: the run to a solar panel needs it) or ac (inverter to AC panel); propane is propane PIPE (a tank to a house connector). Pairs with Wire Length. water is PVC water pipe (docs/WELLS.md); sewer is black waste pipe (a building's waste outlet to its septic system, docs/SEPTIC.md). fuel is a fuel line (a bulk fuel tank to a fuel pump).

panel_offset_m.label: Panel Height (m)
panel_offset_m.note: A solar mount: how far above the mount's origin the fitted panel's underside sits (a roof mount 0.10, a ground rack the height of its low edge plus half the slope).

panel_width_m.label: Panel Width (m)
panel_width_m.note: A solar mount: the width of the panel it takes seen from above. Mounts snap to each other this far apart so the panels do not overlap.

panel_depth_m.label: Panel Depth (m)
panel_depth_m.note: A solar mount: the depth of its panel seen from above (a tilted panel is shorter from above than it is long).

panel_tilt_deg.label: Panel Tilt (deg)
panel_tilt_deg.note: A solar mount: the fitted panel's tilt about the X axis (0 flat on a roof, 30 on a ground rack).

flow_lph.label: Flow (L/h)
flow_lph.note: A submersible well pump: liters an hour it lifts. A well gives this, or what the aquifer under it gives, whichever is less (docs/WELLS.md). On a WATER PIPE (wire_kind water): liters an hour the pipe carries; a water line gives no more than its narrowest pipe lets through (half inch 900, one inch 2400, two inch 9000).

pressurized.label: Pressurized
pressurized.note: A water tank that holds its water under pressure (a pressure tank, a water heater): a building's taps draw from it with no pump running. A plain cistern needs a water pump between it and what it feeds.

heater_w.label: Heater (W)
heater_w.note: A water heater: its element's watts. A water tank (wire_role water_tank) with a heater warms what it holds to 55 C while the building it stands in has power, drawing these watts while it heats.

filter_stage.label: Filter Stage
filter_stage.note: A water filter on a well's water line (wire_role water_filter): water reaching a tank through a sediment, a carbon and a uv stage is clean (drinkable); otherwise it is raw.

is_well.label: Drilled Well
is_well.note: A structure that is a drilled well: its recipe lines may scale with the depth to water (per_depth_m), it takes a sub panel (attach_item) and pumps into the tanks it is piped to.

sewage_capacity_l.label: Septic Capacity (L)
sewage_capacity_l.note: A septic tank structure (wire_role septic_tank): the liters it holds. Sludge builds up in it as the buildings piped to it drain (half as fast through a macerator pump); the liquid flows on to its distribution box and leach fields. Pumped out by the honey pot truck (docs/SEPTIC.md).

leach_lpd.label: Leach Rate (L/day)
leach_lpd.note: A leach field structure (wire_role leach_field): the liters a game day that soak away into the ground from it (docs/SEPTIC.md).

leach_storage_l.label: Leach Storage (L)
leach_storage_l.note: A leach field: the liters its gravel trenches hold while they soak away. When the fields are full the septic system backs up and the fixtures will not drain.

pushable.label: Pushable
pushable.note: The player grabs it by the handles and pushes it along like a wheelbarrow (right click to grab, right click to put down) instead of picking it up. A portable generator is pushed.

power_radius_tiles.label: Power Radius (tiles)
power_radius_tiles.note: A portable generator: it powers everything that needs electricity (not battery powered) within this many tiles of it. It is not connected to structures: a building runs on its own system. Its rated power is max_power_w.

capacity_wh.label: Capacity (Wh)
capacity_wh.note: A battery's energy capacity in watt-hours. Shown by the look-at panel.

voltage_v.label: Voltage (V)
voltage_v.note: A battery's nominal voltage. Shown by the look-at panel.

wire_length_m.label: Wire Length (m)
wire_length_m.note: How many metres of wire the coil or spool holds. Each connection uses the distance between its two devices plus 0.5 m of slack; the game counts the metres used and removes the spool when it is empty.

attach_through.label: Through The Wall
attach_through.note: A wall item (attach_surface wall, either side) that goes THROUGH the wall, like a wire entry: its model has a node 'Plate' (the face plate on the aimed side, its back on the plane y = 0 and its front towards -y in Blender) and a node 'Pipe' (a sleeve 0.25 m long going into the wall, towards +y in Blender). The game measures the wall, lengthens the pipe to it and puts a second plate on the other side, so the item shows and is clicked from both sides. See docs/ATTACHED_ITEMS.md.

net_ports.label: Network Ports
net_ports.note: Network gear (a wire_role that starts net_): how many Cat6 cables it takes. A router: its LAN ports (the dish or yagi that feeds it goes in its WAN port, which is not counted). docs/INTERNET.md.

poe.label: PoE Ports
poe.note: A switch or injector whose ports each give 15 W of DC power over the cable: a camera, an access point or a yagi on one of them needs no other supply.

poe_powered.label: Runs From PoE
poe_powered.note: A network device that takes its power from the cable (a camera, an access point, a yagi): it is cabled only to a PoE port, and everything else only to a standard port.

rack_units.label: Rack Units
rack_units.note: A rackmount router or switch: the units it takes in a wall rack (1). 0 = it does not go in a rack.

rack_capacity_u.label: Rack Capacity (U)
rack_capacity_u.note: A rack (wire_role net_rack): the units it holds. The gear in it is cabled as one device: its ports add up.

sawmill.label: Sawmill
sawmill.note: A placeable stationary sawmill (docs/SAWMILL.md): an uncut log is laid on its track (left click with it in hand), a right click asks what lumber to cut, the carriage makes three passes and the lumber is stacked beside it. The model has the parts SawCarriage, SawBlade and Frame.

roof_mount.label: Also Mounts On A Roof
roof_mount.note: A placeable item that may ALSO be put up on a finished building's roof (a dish, a yagi, an access point): aimed at the roof from the ground it stands upright there, and R turns it 12.5 degrees a press (also once it is up, with the cursor on it). A wrench (Shift + right click) takes it down.

shelf.label: Shelf
shelf.note: A wall item (attach_surface wall) that is a SHELF: items are stood on its top face in a row (left click with the item in hand, right click the item to take it back). The top face is the top of the model bounds; see docs/ATTACHED_ITEMS.md.

attach_item.label: Mount Takes Item
attach_item.note: A mount (a solar rack) takes this item (a solar panel): a right click on the placed mount with the item in hand fits it. Item id; pairs with attach_result. The item itself should not be placeable (placeable false): it only goes on its mount.

attach_result.label: Mount Becomes
attach_result.note: What the mount becomes once its attach_item is fitted (the rack with its panel, a separate item with its own model). It is not for sale; a roof one has attach_surface roof like the mount.

attach_side.label: Mount Side
attach_side.note: For a wall mount: which side of the wall it goes on. interior = inside a room (switches, sconces), exterior = outside the building (a breaker box, a wall lantern), either = both.

provides_power.label: Brings Power
provides_power.note: Mounted on the OUTSIDE of a building it brings electricity to that building (the outdoor breaker box). Lights whose manifest entry says requires_power stay dark in a building without it.

look_target.label: Building Look: Parts
look_target.note: Used as a construction material, this item decides how parts of the building LOOK. One or more of: roof, walls (logs, siding), interior (paint), floor (carpet, tile, flooring), chimney (brick, stone), foundation (see Foundation Style), separated by commas (bricks: "chimney,foundation"). Leave empty for items that do not.

look_color.label: Building Look: Colour
look_color.note: The colour of that part of the building as #RRGGBB (birch logs white-cream, pine warm brown, shingles slate grey).

look_metallic.label: Building Look: Metallic
look_metallic.note: 0 = not metal, 1 = bare metal (a tin roof, steel siding).

look_style.label: Building Look: Foundation Style
look_style.note: For an item whose parts include foundation: the foundation style it builds: poured (the slab), block (concrete block stem wall), brick (brick or stone stem wall, coloured by Look Colour) or stilts (piles under a deck).

burn_minutes.label: Burns For (game minutes)
burn_minutes.note: Fuel for a fireplace: placed in a fireplace (right click the chimney of a finished building with it) it burns for this many game minutes. 0 = not a fireplace fuel.

lights_fires.label: Lights Fires
lights_fires.note: A lighter or match: right click a fireplace that has fuel in it with this item in hand to light the fire. It is not used up.

fence_style.label: Fence Style
fence_style.note: A fence material the player builds with: wood (post and rail) or wire. With it in hand each click places a post; the panels fill in between the posts when the fence is built.

fence_panel_m.label: Fence Panel Length (m)
fence_panel_m.note: How far one panel of this fencing reaches between two posts; a run of L metres uses ceil(L / this) panels.

fence_height_m.label: Fence Height (m)
fence_height_m.note: How tall the finished fence stands.

fence_post_item.label: Fence Post Item
fence_post_item.note: The item id of the post this fencing is built on (one per post, taken from the hotbar when the fence is built).

gate_width_m.label: Gate Width (m)
gate_width_m.note: A gate: with it in hand, a click on a built fence takes the fence out for this width and stands the gate in the gap. Empty = not a gate.

gate_style.label: Gate Style
gate_style.note: How the gate looks: wood or metal.

path_kind.label: Path / Road Kind
path_kind.note: A surface the player lays as a smooth curved route (PathBuilder): path (narrow, for walking) or road (wide, for vehicles). Empty = not a path material.

path_width_m.label: Path Width (m)
path_width_m.note: How wide the laid surface is (paths about 1.2 m, roads about 4 m).

path_style.label: Path Surface
path_style.note: How the surface looks. Asphalt also gets a centre lane marking.

path_m_per_item.label: Metres Per Item
path_m_per_item.note: How many metres of route one item lays; a route of L metres uses ceil(L / this) items.

is_blueprint.label: Blueprint
is_blueprint.note: Bought once, starts a build when held (structure site, path or road route) and is never used up. Shown on the blueprint blue (#35637C). Structures that build in stages are blueprints automatically.

path_material_item.label: Path Material Item
path_material_item.note: On a path or road blueprint: the item id of the material it lays (one per path_m_per_item metres), taken from the hotbar or the work site.
